purpose: Cinematic scientific illustration, Sun-to-Earth chapter; historical visual references rather than live observation.

general_usage_policy.summary: NASA media is generally not subject to US copyright unless a third-party copyright owner is identified; credit NASA. Commercial uses must not imply NASA endorsement. NASA logos, employee likenesses and other protected identifiers have separate rules. These texture files contain geography/clouds, not NASA logos or people. No NASA endorsement is claimed.

day.title: Blue Marble: Next Generation, July 2004 base map
day.creator: Reto Stöckli, NASA Earth Observatory (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center)
day.acquisition_period: July 2004 monthly composite; MODIS land observations
day.image_specific_terms: BMNG project page requests NASA Earth Observatory credit for use or republication. No third-party copyright exception is identified for this selected base-map image in the project/download record.
day.factual_limits: Historical composite, not current satellite imagery. Cloud removal and polar fill are composite processing. Deep ocean uses a uniform authored blue in the NASA source, not measured bathymetry or an observation of every water pixel. Base variant selected to avoid pre-baked topographic shading.

clouds.title: Blue Marble: Clouds (2002 release)
clouds.creator: Reto Stöckli, NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; enhancements credited to Robert Simmon
clouds.credit: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center / Reto Stöckli; enhancements by Robert Simmon
clouds.acquisition_period: Historical Blue Marble cloud composite; publication February 11, 2002. Source description says two days of visible imagery with a third day of thermal infrared imagery over the poles; exact observation dates not specified in the selected record.
clouds.image_specific_terms: The NASA Visible Earth record describes these images as freely available to educators, scientists, museums and the public. The selected record credits NASA creators and identifies no third-party copyright restriction.
clouds.verification_limit: The former Visible Earth content now redirects to the Earth Observatory home page. Image-specific description/credit were verified from the search-index copy of the official NASA record on 2026-09-08; the exact image itself remains accessible on the official eoimages.gsfc.nasa.gov host and was downloaded successfully. Generic NASA usage policy was verified live.
clouds.factual_limits: Independent historical cloud composite, not the weather for July 2004 and not live weather. This layer is used illustratively and can be gently rotated by the renderer; do not describe the full rendered globe as a single dated observation.

memory_notes: Estimates assume browser RGBA8 decoded images and Three.js RGBA8 textures with a full generated mip chain. They exclude driver overhead, render targets, geometry, copies and browser cache. WebP is transfer compression, not GPU block compression; actual allocations must be measured in target runtime.
coordinate_notes: Both image rasters are north-up full equirectangular: left -180°, center Greenwich 0°, right +180°; top +90°, bottom -90°. No image rotation/flip has been baked. With standard Three SphereGeometry and TextureLoader flipY=true, Greenwich maps to local +X, 90°E to local -Z, north to +Y. Britain near lon -2°, lat 54° is approximately direction (0.587, 0.809, 0.0205) before mesh rotation. If camera is on +Z, rotate globe Y=-pi/2 to bring Greenwich front; camera elevation/tilt then brings Europe into view. Confirm with an actual rendered frame.
delivery: Copy only four root .webp files into served assets. Keep sources/ outside served build. Copy provenance files into project documentation. Optimization script is reproducible with Pillow WebP support.
